title: Mirabel and the Ghost
premise: Lior Sterling, a burned-out private security contractor, is hired to shadow a nervous tech executive on a transatlantic flight—then the flight's records vanish mid-air, along with every passenger manifest, while she watches from the tarmac. Digging in to prove the plane existed, she uncovers a coordinated erasure spanning three governments, and realizes the 'ghost flight' carried something—or someone—that powerful people need forgotten. Hunted by an assassin who was on the same payroll, Lior must smuggle a surviving passenger's testimony across a border whose checkpoint rosters change at dawn, choosing between the loyalty that once defined her and the truth that could free her from the incident that broke her sleep. She gets the testimony through at terrible cost, exposes the conspiracy, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Noor Okafor is a former aviation logistics analyst who spent a decade tracking cargo manifests across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the paper trails powerful people would rather burn.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She takes a last-minute contract guarding tech executive Mara Voss on a red-eye flight, noting the client's paranoia and the odd payment structure. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking dread—Lior hasn't slept properly since 'the incident' and takes jobs to avoid being alone with her thoughts.

chapters.title: Red-Eye
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, split with brief airport CCTV excerpts. She watches Mara board, then is pulled aside by a 'customs' officer who is clearly not customs. By the time she breaks free, the plane has departed. Emotional beat: the first crack of wrongness—something about the delay felt orchestrated.

chapters.title: Vanished
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The flight number returns no results. The airline denies the booking; the airport system shows an empty slot. Her own contract file has been altered to remove Mara's name. Emotional beat: gaslit vertigo—Lior doubts her own memory for the first time since the incident.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She reconstructs evidence from parking receipts, a barista who served Mara, and her own photos, building a physical dossier. Someone ransacks her apartment but takes only the contract copy. Emotional beat: stubborn resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Manifest
chapters.summary: New POV: Elias Brandt, the assassin, briefed by an unseen handler to find 'the contractor who saw the boarding.' He reviews Lior's file and finds the incident that ended her military career. Emotional beat: cold curiosity—Brandt begins to wonder why Lior was allowed to live.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following a lead to a coastal safehouse, she finds Tomas Reyes, a flight engineer who was aboard and bailed before takeoff via crew door. He's terrified, injured, and carrying a data drive he won't explain. Emotional beat: wary alliance—two people who shouldn't trust anyone trusting each other.

chapters.title: What the Drive Holds
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, flashback-heavy. The flight carried a defector with proof of a shared surveillance program across three governments; the 'vanishing' was a negotiated erasure. Emotional beat: the weight of knowing—Tomas has been running for six days on adrenaline and guilt.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She contacts an old intelligence contact, Ade, who maps the conspiracy's shape and warns her that all three governments would rather kill her than admit the flight existed. Emotional beat: the scale of the wall she's chosen to climb.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Old Address
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with flashbacks to the incident. Her former unit commander, Rennick—now a private-sector fixer—offers her protection and a quiet life if she hands over Tomas. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme crystallizes; the offer is genuinely tempting.

chapters.title: Safehouse Falling
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Brandt POV. Brandt finds the safehouse; Lior and Tomas escape through fishing sheds as it burns. Tomas is grazed; the drive survives. Emotional beat: survival high curdling into the knowledge that they can never stop moving.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint Clock
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Ade explains the only window: the northern border checkpoint changes shift rosters at dawn, and the new roster includes a name loyal to the conspiracy. They have until 5 a.m. Emotional beat: a countdown begins, ticking under everything.

chapters.title: Rennick's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Pressured by his own handlers, he sets a trap disguised as an extraction offer, genuinely believing he's saving Lior from herself. Emotional beat: tragic self-deception—Rennick still thinks of himself as her protector.

chapters.title: The Meeting
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She meets Rennick alone, wearing a wire, and lets him reveal the operation's scope on tape before walking out. Emotional beat: grief—she records the man who once pulled her out of a burning vehicle.

chapters.title: Brandt's Doubt
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Reviewing the erased flight's cargo logs, he finds his own name listed among the crew of a flight he never flew—evidence he was meant to die aboard it too. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he's prey.

chapters.title: An Uneasy Truce
chapters.summary: Lior and Brandt POV, alternating. Brandt corners Lior, then instead offers what he knows: the defector's proof is only half the drive's contents; the other half names every operative, including him. Emotional beat: enemies bound by mutual exposure.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The group drives through the night toward the border while Ade's network is rolled up in real time—his last message is a warning, then silence. Tomas's wound turns septic. Emotional beat: mounting dread; the clock and the fever both rising.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Dawn
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, real-time. At the checkpoint they split: Brandt creates a diversion as himself, deliberately surrendering to draw the roster loyalist away. Lior walks Tomas through the shift change in the gap. Emotional beat: sacrifice—Brandt buys the truth with his freedom.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. In custody, he trades the operative list for a delayed transfer, buying Lior hours. His handler arrives to silence him; Brandt escapes into the border town's maze. Emotional beat: a killer choosing a side, with no illusions about surviving it.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. From a border-town internet café, she and Tomas release the drive to a distributed network of journalists Ade pre-arranged, timed so no single government can suppress it. Emotional beat: exhale and terror—the truth is out and can never be pulled back.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Rennick, exposed by the tape and the drive, confronts her one last time—not with a gun, but with the question of whether she'd have done the same for the unit. She says yes; that's why she had to do this. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme resolves not in victory but in understanding.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief. Hearings begin in two countries; the third stalls and its minister resigns anyway. Tomas testifies; Brandt disappears into witness protection under a name Lior will never learn. Emotional beat: partial justice, honestly rendered—erasure undone by testimony.

chapters.title: The First Quiet Morning
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Months later, Lior sleeps through the night and wakes without reaching for a weapon. She takes a small, honest contract guarding a school, and mails Mara Voss's recovered boarding photo to the memorial wall built for the erased flight. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a unit or a cause, but in the choice to keep telling the truth.
